headline: Your final height
subhead: IS DECIDED BY ONE CELL TYPE
body: A thin layer of stem cells sitting right at the top of the growth plate.
punch: Everything under them is just the production line they feed.

headline: They're called
body: The name is misleading. They're not resting, they're the reserve. They divide slowly, and every division produces the columns of chondrocytes that actually make the bone longer.
punch: They're not idle. They're being spent.

headline: And they run out
body: In rabbits, over 95% of resting zone cells were dividing at birth. By 17 weeks that dropped under 10%. The cell count fell too, not just the activity.
punch: Fewer cells and less active. It empties both ways.

headline: We now know
body: They're marked by PTHrP. Single cell sequencing of human pubertal growth plate biopsies confirmed the same two populations exist in people, not just mice.
punch: This stopped being a mouse story in 2025.

headline: Switch them on
body: One Hedgehog agonist bead implanted in a single rat femur produced a measurable, growing length difference against the untreated leg on the same animal.
punch: Same animal, same genetics, one leg longer.

headline: They also need
body: These cells only stay stem like in a low Wnt environment. Force canonical Wnt signalling on and they lose the ability to form columns at all.
punch: The niche isn't background. It's a requirement.

headline: And growth hormone
body: GH stimulates human resting zone cells through JAK/STAT and local TGF beta, completely separate from the liver IGF-1 pathway everyone talks about.
punch: The GH story has a second half nobody covers.

headline: But here's the gap
body: Nobody has directly tested whether normal fusion is these cells clonally exhausting themselves. It's the best model we have and it's still inference.
punch: Best available explanation is not the same as proven.
